a.summary: `@Deprecated(forRemoval = true)` is applied to the abstract `sign(SequencedCollection<Signer>)`, which implementors cannot stop implementing; honoring the removal later silently rebinds `signInOrder(SequencedCollection)`'s body from positional to by-key signing rather than failing to compile.
a.failure_scenario: Two concrete failures. (a) Today: a third-party implementor sees `[removal] sign(SequencedCollection<Signer>) in Transaction has been deprecated and marked for removal`, deletes the override as instructed, and gets `error: MyTx is not abstract and does not override abstract method sign(SequencedCollection<Signer>)`. There is no way to comply — the warning is unactionable, and MIGRATION.md's closing paragraph ("New instance methods have defaults, so existing Transaction implementations do not need additional method overrides") addresses only the additions and never mentions the deprecated abstract method they are forced to keep. (b) At the promised removal: line 846's unchanged body `sign(signers)` still compiles, because `SequencedCollection<Signer>` is a `Collection<Signer>`, and silently retargets to the by-key `sign(Collection)`. I verified this — with the `SequencedCollection` overload deleted, javac emits `invokeinterface sign:(Ljava/util/Collection;)V` with no error and no warning. `signInOrder` would then sign by public key while its javadoc at 838-843 still promises "the first signer writes the first signature slot regardless of its public key". Notably, the sibling bodies at 851/856/861/866/871 would all fail to compile on removal, so this is the one entry point whose breakage is silent.

b.summary: Eight of the nine new `signInOrder*` methods are implemented by calling the very methods this commit marks `forRemoval`, so the deprecation cannot be honoured by deletion.
b.failure_scenario: A future maintainer executes the removal the annotations promise and deletes the nine deprecated members. Every `signInOrder*` replacement loses its body simultaneously: the static at line 706 calls the deprecated static `sign(signers, out, msgOffset, msgLen, sigOffset)` (deprecated at 648), line 717 calls deprecated `sign(signers, out)` (663), and the instance defaults at 846, 851, 856, 861, 866 and 871 call the deprecated `sign(SequencedCollection)` (783), `signAndBase64Encode(SequencedCollection)` (790), `sign(byte[],SequencedCollection)` (800), `sign(String,SequencedCollection)` (810) and the two `signAndBase64Encode(hash, ...)` overloads (821, 832). The 846 case is the sharpest: `signInOrder(SequencedCollection)` delegates to the deprecated *abstract* `sign(SequencedCollection)`, which is the only hook any implementation provides — removing it leaves the replacement with no implementation to reach and turns a deletion into a re-plumbing of `BaseTransaction` and every third-party implementor. MIGRATION.md's closing claim that 'New instance methods have defaults, so existing `Transaction` implementations do not need additional method overrides' is true only for as long as the deprecated abstract method survives, which the annotation says it will not.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
